title: Wren and the Vow
premise: Silas Okonkwo has built her career on erasure, ghostwriting the memoirs of celebrated rival author Marguerite Vale while keeping her own name off every page. When she inherits a half-share of a failing orchard from the grandmother who raised her, she discovers the deed's other name belongs to Wren Ashby, the man she loved and abandoned twelve years ago to protect him from her family's debts. Forced to share the orchard through one final growing season before developers raze it, Silas and Wren strip away old lies: he learns she left to save him, and she learns his silence was its own kind of vow. As Marguerite threatens to expose Silas's ghostwriting and seize the orchard in a contractual trap, Silas must publish under her own name at last. The book ends with the orchard saved by the sales of Silas's first novel, and Wren staying past the last train, choosing love over the duty that once divided them.
about_author: Bram Montrose is the pen name of a former orchard worker turned novelist who spent a decade writing other people's stories before claiming her own. She lives between a cider town and a city library, where she still reads deeds for pleasure.

chapters.title: The Invisible Hand
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. In a Manhattan hotel suite, Silas ghosts the final chapters of Marguerite Vale's memoir while Marguerite performs gratitude for cameras. Silas returns to her apartment and finds a lawyer's letter about an inherited orchard. Beat: competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Two Names on Paper
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. In the county records office, Silas discovers the deed names Wren Ashby as co-owner. Panic and vertigo; she hasn't spoken to him since the night she vanished. Beat: the past arriving with legal force.

chapters.title: What the Grandmother Kept
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Sorting her grandmother's farmhouse, Silas finds unsent letters addressed to Wren and a ledger showing debts her family hid from him. She understands why she was sent away. Beat: grief reframing guilt.

chapters.title: The Man Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, now the orchard's reluctant caretaker, prunes trees he never planted and refuses to answer the lawyer's letters. He sees a stranger's car on the road. Beat: stubbornness as armor.

chapters.title: First Frost Meeting
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Silas arrives at the orchard; Wren mistakes her for a developer's surveyor until she speaks. Twelve years collapse into one hostile conversation about selling. Beat: anger as the only safe intimacy.

chapters.title: Terms of Coexistence
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They negotiate a season: if the harvest fails to cover taxes, both sign the sale. Wren sets rules designed to keep her at arm's length, then breaks his own rule lending her his grandmother's coat. Beat: grudging truce.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Leash
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Marguerite calls, revealing a contract clause giving her publisher first claim on any book Silas writes for two years, and hints she knows about the orchard. Silas realizes her invisibility is a cage. Beat: dread tightening.

chapters.title: Pruning Lessons
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren teaches Silas to prune; she cuts too deep, he guides her hands, and neither pulls away. He almost asks why she left, then doesn't. Beat: tenderness breaking through routine.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas plans to leave after signing papers, but misses the last train on purpose after finding Wren asleep over tax documents. She stays the night in the farmhouse, telling herself it's practical. Beat: self-deception cracking.

chapters.title: Cider and Confessions
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Pressing apples late into the night, Wren finally demands the truth. Silas admits her father's creditors would have taken everything Wren had, including him. His fury breaks into something rawer. Beat: the wound opened.

chapters.title: What Silence Cost Him
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confesses his side: he waited two winters, then stopped waiting, and let the orchard become his whole life so he'd have nothing left to lose. Beat: mutual recognition of damage.

chapters.title: A Kiss Against Duty
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. After a storm knocks out power, they shelter in the barn and kiss. Silas pulls back, citing the sale agreement and Marguerite's leash. Wren calls her a coward, gently. Beat: desire versus fear.

chapters.title: The Developer's Offer
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A developer doubles his offer, enough to erase Wren's debts entirely. Tempted, he hides the letter from Silas, repeating her old sin of deciding alone. Beat: corruption of good intentions.

chapters.title: Marguerite Arrives
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Marguerite visits the orchard uninvited, offering to buy Silas's share and bury the ghostwriting scandal, provided Silas signs away her next book. Silas refuses for the first time in her career. Beat: spine found.

chapters.title: The Exposé
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Marguerite leaks Silas's ghostwriting to the press. Wren learns his lover's entire public identity was a fiction and feels the old abandonment echo. He gives her space; she hears it as rejection. Beat: lowest point approaching.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve Fight
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. On the eve of harvest, Wren confronts Silas about the hidden developer letter and her hidden life. She accuses him of loving the orchard more than any person. Both say unforgivable true things. Beat: rupture.

chapters.title: Alone Among Trees
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas works the harvest alone while Wren drinks in town. She drafts a resignation from ghostwriting and a first chapter of her own novel, titled 'Wren.' Beat: choosing voice over safety.

chapters.title: The Letter He Never Sent
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Sobering up, Wren finds his grandmother's copy of the deed and a note revealing Silas's grandmother paid off his debts secretly all those years ago. Her exile was a sacrifice, not a betrayal. Beat: reversal of judgment.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Orchard
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A hailstorm threatens the crop on harvest day. Wren and Silas work side by side through the night saving what they can, wordless, hands bleeding, old anger burned away by shared labor. Beat: reconciliation through action.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas publishes her own manuscript independently, exposing Marguerite's contract trap publicly. The scandal reverses onto Marguerite; the publisher drops the claim on the orchard. Beat: climax, power answered with truth.

chapters.title: The Deed Rewritten
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Harvest numbers come in just short of the tax bill, but preorders of Silas's novel close the gap. At the lawyer's office they amend the deed together, then tear up the sale agreement. Beat: victory earned jointly.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Winter settles over the orchard. Silas's book launches; Wren reads it in the farmhouse kitchen. The last train passes without either of them leaving. He asks her to stay; she says she already has. Beat: love chosen over duty, home made.
